claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy's strength and ductility are below industrial fastener requirements.
The starting alloy's creep performance is below industrial fastener requirements.
The starting alloy has substandard corrosion performance for fastener applications.
The proposed intervention is solution treatment at approximately 1200°C for 1 hour, rapid quenching, and aging at 600–650°C for 10–20 hours under an inert atmosphere.
The proposed heat treatment will form uniformly distributed nanoscale B2-ordered precipitates without disrupting the lamellar architecture.
The nanoscale B2 precipitates will pin dislocations.
Precipitation hardening from the proposed treatment will increase yield strength.
The precipitates will reduce grain-boundary sliding and thereby improve creep resistance.
The precipitates will stabilize the microstructure during deformation and thermal cycling.
Precipitation will modify local interface chemistry in a manner that enhances corrosion resistance.
The treatment will increase yield strength by more than 20–30% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will increase creep resistance by more than 20–30% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will improve resistance to fatigue-crack initiation and propagation.
The treatment will improve corrosion performance under extreme temperature fluctuations.
The expected benefits apply from -40°C to 300°C under long-term fastener loads and representative industrial corrosive environments.
Temperatures outside the stated range or deviations from the optimized treatment can cause over-aging or microstructural instability.
The long-term stability of the precipitate distribution under prolonged cyclic loading and corrosive attack is uncertain.
The controlled experiment compares heat-treated and untreated fine-lamellar fastener components under identical thermal, mechanical, and corrosive exposures.

The hypothesis is falsified if the treatment fails to provide at least 20% improvements in both yield strength and creep resistance, or produces no measurable improvement in corrosion resistance and fatigue performance.
